data.body:
LEAF b0ac silverish-parodic-quoll — phases 4a-4d.

4a CENSUS: the mechanism is 'concurrent writers to one logical target'. Slots: CLI/MCP/library are
OUT OF SCOPE as proving surfaces — the property under change is ATOMICITY of an internal write, not
a surface semantic, and driving it from a surface would not cross the faulty seam any better.
AUTOMATED CALLERS in scope and important: review_bot/reconcile.py's cursor is written by the review
bot, and _opcert_signing's pid-derived temp collides across THREADS in the threaded MCP server.
DUAL-DIRECTION in scope: the read side (torn read) is exactly what the two no-temp sites expose.

4b RED-FIRST, 20 tests. Design note worth keeping: current and fixed code publish through DIFFERENT
seams (Path.replace vs fsutil's os.replace), so a barrier alone would give a FLAKY red. I paired a
DETERMINISTIC adoption assertion (structural — legitimate here because adoption IS the contract per
AC2/AC5) with the barriered concurrency test that proves the property.
RESULT 11 FAILED / 9 passed, all right-reason:
  6x hazard site still hand-rolls its write (adoption)
  4x site derives a temp name from its target (janitor+banking correctly PASS — they have no temp
     at all, they are the non-atomic pair)
  1x THE REAL DEFECT REPRODUCED DETERMINISTICALLY:
     'a concurrent cursor write was silently dropped: [reconcile_cursor_write_error]'
Better than designed: patching fsutil.os.replace patches the GLOBAL os module object, and
pathlib.Path.replace delegates to os.replace, so the barrier engaged against the UNCONVERTED code
too. The production race is therefore provable now, not only after the fix.
9 passing = happy path (4), negative control (distinct targets unaffected), atomic_write's own
two-writer and atomicity properties (fsutil is already correct), and the 2 no-derivation cases for
the no-temp sites.

4c HELD OUT tests/unit/test_unique_cache_writes_heldout.py (moved to job tmp). Implementer sees only
4 round-trip happy-path tests.
4d DISPATCHED with: the six sites and their exact current shapes, the instruction to REUSE
fsutil.atomic_write and add no new module, per-site error-path preservation notes, the thread-vs-
process subtlety for _opcert_signing, and the binding lint/typecheck/complexity/module-size gates.

STACK: 2503 (8ce5) -> 2504 (f9b9). b0ac will be third.
